Question: What do British people mean when they say they want to "get a skip to put stuff in" or what is a "skip"?
Answer: If you are American, think “roll-off dumpster.” They are huge metal boxes intended for removal of waste in projects. They are, in the U.K., traditionally coloured bright yellow. (although there are now more colour choices available). They come in a range of standard sizes, from 6’ and upwards in length. They don’t have lids, so that a pile of empty ones can be stacked. Typically, you don’t own one, but rent one from a licensed company for the duration of a project. The rental fee includes delivery of the empty skip, removal of the full skip, and environmentally legal disposal of the contents. There are some things, like asbestos, that you’re not allowed to put in one.

Question: Are you shocked like me by the parody of the Last Supper by drag queens for the Paris Olympics because it violates the Olympic rules of not doing ideological militantism?
Answer: As a Christian, I loved it. Okay, it appears that it was primarily inspired by a Flemish painting of Greek gods. I find it a bit hard to believe that no-one on the design team had thought “Hang on a minute doesn’t this feel a bit like a parody of a famous piece of Christian art?” So I’m going to treat it as if the team knew that that reference would be drawn and were happy with it. So my considered theological view is as follows. If you can’t see the face of Christ in a drag queen, you’re not looking hard enough.
